# Keyfold: full description

Keyfold is a self-hosted secrets vault for one person: it keeps passwords, API tokens, SSH passphrases and notes encrypted with age on the operator's own machine, with a web UI, a command line tool (kf) and an MCP server for AI agents.

- Product page: https://keyfold.pulseview.app/ (French), https://keyfold.pulseview.app/en (English)
- Source code: https://github.com/dev-toolings/Keyfold
- Reference documentation: the README at the root of the repository

## Who it is for

One operator (a developer or a system administrator) who wants their secrets on hardware they control, and who needs scripts, programs and AI agents to use those secrets without printing them. It is not a team or family password manager: there is one vault, one master password, and no sharing between users.

## Components

- `keyfold-server`: a Go HTTP server. It stores encrypted files in a data directory (`./data` by default) and listens on `127.0.0.1:8717` by default. It can also serve the built web UI.
- `kf`: a Go command line tool. It talks to the server, keeps the vault unlocked through a local agent, and includes an MCP server (`kf mcp`).
- Web UI: a React single page app. `/` and `/en` are the public product page; the vault app lives under `/personal` (unlock, dashboard, vault, health, settings).

All three share one vault. The HTTP API is versioned under `/api/v1`.

## How encryption works

- Encryption is client side only, with age (https://age-encryption.org). The Go code uses `filippo.io/age`; the browser uses the `age-encryption` TypeScript package. A test suite checks that both produce files the other can read.
- The vault identity is an X25519 age key. It is encrypted with the master password through the age scrypt recipient (scrypt work factor logN 18).
- Each item, its name included, is a separate age file encrypted to that identity. Attachments are encrypted in the browser with age too, and stored apart in `data/blobs/`.
- The server never receives the master password, the identity or a secret value. It sees ciphertext only.
- A new vault needs a master password of at least 16 characters. The encrypted identity can be downloaded by anyone who reaches the server (it exposes no more than a stolen disk would), so the master password is the barrier against an offline attack.
- Optional second factor (TOTP): with it on, the encrypted identity is only handed out against a valid code. A code works once; five wrong codes in a row lock every check for 15 minutes. The TOTP secret is stored in clear on the server (`data/totp.json`, mode 0600), so TOTP does not protect a stolen disk.
- API access needs a session token, obtained by decrypting a random challenge with the identity. Tokens live in server memory only (15 minutes idle expiry): a server restart locks every client.
- Changing the master password re-wraps the same identity; items are not re-encrypted.

## What an item holds

Kinds: `login` (default), `token`, `note`, `identity`, `ssh-key`, `ssh-passphrase`. An item can hold an identifier, the secret, web addresses, a TOTP secret, custom fields (hidden or not), a note, a folder, a favorite flag, attachments (up to 100 MiB each by default, set by `keyfold-server -max-blob`) and its 20 previous values, each one restorable.

## Command line (kf)

The server URL comes from `-server`, then the `KEYFOLD_SERVER` environment variable, then `http://127.0.0.1:8717`.

- `kf init`: asks the master password twice and creates the vault.
- `kf unlock [-ttl 1h]`: decrypts the identity and starts a background agent on a `0600` socket in a `0700` directory. The identity reaches the agent through a pipe, never argv or environment.
- `kf lock`: stops the agent.
- `kf get <name>`: prints the value to stdout. Refused when stdout is a terminal, so a secret is not shown on screen by accident.
- `kf set <name> [-kind K] [-note N]`: reads the value from stdin. The old value goes to the item history.
- `kf read kf://<name>/<field>`: prints one field (`value`, `username`, `note`, `url`, `totp` or a custom field). Refused on a terminal.
- `kf run -env VAR=kf://<name>/<field> [-env ...] -- cmd [args]`: runs `cmd` with the secrets in its environment, never in argv or on disk.
- `kf inject -i template [-o out]`: replaces every `{{ kf://name/field }}` in a template. The output file is written with mode `0600`.
- `kf generate [-len 24] [-symbols=false] [-words N]`: prints a random password, or a passphrase from the EFF large wordlist. Stores nothing.
- `kf totp <name>`: prints the item's current TOTP code.
- `kf export [-format keyfold|bitwarden-json] [-o file] (-encrypt | -plaintext)`: exports every item. `-encrypt` writes an age file protected by a passphrase of at least 16 characters; plaintext must be asked for explicitly. Attachments are left out.
- `kf import -format keyfold|bitwarden-json|1password-1pux|csv <file>`: adds the items of an export. CSV reads the Chrome, Firefox, Bitwarden and 1Password headers. Items already present are skipped; payment cards are skipped and listed.
- `kf list`: names and kinds, never values.
- `kf rm <name>`: deletes an item and its attachments.
- `kf migrate [-apply]`: rewrites items stored in an older format.

Example, start a program with its database password and no `.env` file:

    kf run -env DB_PASSWORD=kf://prod-db/password -- ./server

## MCP server for AI agents

`kf mcp` serves three tools over stdin/stdout, through the local agent (run `kf unlock` first):

- `list_items`: name, kind, creation and last modification dates of each item.
- `generate_item`: creates an item holding a random secret generated and encrypted locally. It refuses a name that already exists.
- `vault_health`: server facts (item and attachment counts, sizes, free disk space, TOTP on or off, open sessions) and the dashboard indicators (stale, reused, short, weak, website without TOTP) as item names.

No-secret guarantee: no tool returns a value or a note, and no tool edits or deletes an item. Whatever a tool returns enters the model's conversation and its transcripts, so values stay out by design. An agent that needs a secret for a program uses `kf run` or `kf inject` instead.

Registration in Claude Code: `claude mcp add keyfold -- /path/to/bin/kf mcp`.

## Web UI

- Vault: create, edit and search items; a full item sheet with history, TOTP code and countdown, custom fields and attachments.
- Generator: 24 character passwords or 6 word EFF passphrases.
- A copied secret is cleared from the clipboard after 30 seconds.
- Dashboard: items to renew, reused values, short passwords, weak passwords (estimated entropy under 60 bits), websites without a TOTP secret. All computed in the browser.
- Breach check against Have I Been Pwned: off by default; once allowed in Settings, it runs on request and sends only the first 5 characters of each password's SHA-1 (k-anonymity range API).
- Health page: what the server stores, as seen from ciphertext only.
- Settings: TOTP second factor and master password change.

The web UI keeps the identity and the session token in memory only.

## Import and export formats

- Import: Keyfold's own format (`kf`), Bitwarden JSON (`bitwarden-json`), 1Password export (`1password-1pux`), CSV (Chrome, Firefox, Bitwarden and 1Password headers).
- Export: `kf` or `bitwarden-json`, either encrypted with age (passphrase) or plaintext when asked for explicitly.
- Import and export are available in the CLI only, not in the web UI.

## Self-hosting

- One Go module and one Bun workspace at the repository root. `make build` builds `bin/kf` and `bin/keyfold-server`; `make help` lists every target.
- Run the server: `go run ./apps/keyfold-server -listen 127.0.0.1:8717 -data ./data -web ./apps/web/dist`.
- Logs are JSON lines with a request ID; only method, path, status and duration are logged, never a header, body or query string.
- Recovery when the TOTP phone is lost: `keyfold-server -disable-totp -data ./data` on the server machine.

## Limits and what it does not do yet

- No TLS: the server speaks plain HTTP and must stay on 127.0.0.1.
- No service unit, container image or reverse proxy setup.
- No backup of the data directory.
- Exports leave attachments out.
- No browser extension, no autofill, no mobile app, no sharing between users.
- The repository has no license file yet.
